methodology: Every insight cites the specific ratio/period pair it is derived from in ratios_timeseries.json and quarterly/<YEAR>_Q4.json (or, since 2026-08-27, quarterly/<YEAR>_Q1.json/_Q2.json/_Q3.json). All figures verified programmatically against the written JSON files before this file was finalized. Equity is positive in every year of the series (minimum 6,956.44m in FY2011), so the negative-equity-breaks-ROE trap does not apply to this bank; ROE/ROA are calculated on period-end (not average) PAT/equity/assets throughout. Q1-Q3 quarterly entries are Solo basis from FY2015-Q2 onward (matching the annual series) and Consolidated basis for FY2011 through FY2015-Q1 plus the single-quarter exception FY2023-Q1, always explicitly flagged in that quarter's own period_note -- see sources.json.

risk_signals.statement: The FY2024 asset-quality shock (classified investments 13,797.16m->59,686.20m, described in the recognition-without-provisioning risk_signal below) was completely invisible in this bank's own interim Q1-Q3 2024 filings, now added to this dataset. Provision charge ran at a steady, unremarkable discrete-quarter pace through the first nine months (Q1 301.11m, Q2 371.11m, Q3 361.64m -- averaging 344.62m/quarter) while operating profit before provision kept ACCELERATING every quarter (discrete Q1 650.95m, Q2 818.82m, Q3 878.49m) and cumulative PAT grew steadily and unremarkably (110.85m -> 267.91m -> 460.91m through Q3, i.e. nothing resembling a warning sign). The entire shock hit in Q4 alone: full-year provision charge of 2,053.80m (FY2024 annual report, this dataset's own 2024_Q4.json) implies a discrete Q4 provision charge of 1,019.94m -- 2.96x the Q1-Q3 quarterly average, and by itself almost exactly equal to the entire first nine months combined (1,033.86m). Q4 alone also delivered the year's strongest discrete operating profit before provision (1,683.64m, exceeding any single prior quarter), which is what allowed full-year PAT to still rise to 812.58m (discrete Q4 PAT 351.67m, also the year's highest single quarter) despite absorbing the provisioning surge. Conclusion: an analyst relying only on this bank's own Q1-Q3 2024 interim filings would have seen accelerating, unremarkable profitability quarter over quarter, with zero visible warning of the classified-investment quadrupling disclosed only in the year-end audited accounts -- the FY2024 recognition event was a genuine year-end cliff-edge, not a gradually-emerging trend.

Classified investments (NPIs) jumped 4.33x in one year, from 13,797.16m (FY2023) to 59,686.20m (FY2024), taking the NPL ratio from 7.27% to 29.96% (both self-calculated as classified_loans/gross_loans; the bank's own reported figures are 7.12%/38.91%-coverage for FY2023 and 29.31% NPL for FY2024, consistent with the same picture). Provision for Classified Investments rose only from 5,368m to 7,829m over the same period - far short of the increase in exposure - so Gross NPI coverage collapsed from 38.91% to 13.12% (both figures reproduce exactly against the bank's own reported 'Gross NPI Coverage' ratios for these two years). The resulting unprovided classified-investment balance (59,686.20m - 7,829m = 51,857.20m) is 2.80x the bank's entire FY2024 Solo shareholders' equity (18,535.90m) - i.e. a full write-down of the unprovided exposure would wipe out equity nearly three times over. General Provision for Unclassified Investments has been nil since FY2021 (four consecutive years, FY2021-FY2024), removing what would ordinarily be a buffer against exactly this kind of shock.

Despite the FY2024 asset-quality collapse, reported Solo CRAR barely moved (14.01% at FY2023 to 14.12% at FY2024, both comfortably above the 12.5%-with-buffer requirement) - but the FY2024 annual report's own Directors' Report discloses this is only because 'Bangladesh Bank allowed us deferral... for finalizing the audited accounts without adjusting shortfall provisions where classified investments and its corresponding claims... has not been considered', under which CRAR would otherwise be stated as 15.65% (Solo); the bank's own formal Pillar-3 disclosure states the shortfall-inclusive figure of 14.12% used here. Combined with the nil general-provisioning noted above and the 13.12% coverage ratio, the stable headline CRAR is a case of capital-ratio stability driven by deferred recognition rather than genuine loss-absorption capacity - the same recognition-vs-deferral pattern flagged for ISLAMIBANK and NBL in the sector-wide FY2024 analysis (_HANDOFF.md).

NPL ratio more than doubled in a single year, from 3.64% (FY2016) to 8.29% (FY2017, self-calculated; the bank's own contemporaneous-vintage table reported 8.44%), as classified loans rose from 3,799m to 10,451m. The bank then ground this down over four years to 4.87% by FY2020 (a figure independently confirmed verbatim in that year's own Directors' Report: 'to retain the non-performing loan within 4.87% i.e. Tk. 7,764.22') before asset quality began deteriorating again from FY2021 (6.19%) through FY2022 (7.94%) and FY2023 (7.27%) on the way to the FY2024 shock described above - i.e. FY2024 was the culmination of a renewed deterioration already visible for three years, not a single-year surprise.

Solo ROE fell almost every year from 19.59% (FY2011) to a series-low 4.00% (FY2021) even as the bank nearly tripled in size (Total Assets 74,704.36m to 223,348.48m over the same span) - ROA fell in parallel from 1.82% to 0.31%. ROE partially recovered to 7.39% by FY2023 (PAT 1,360.72m, a series-high in absolute terms) before relapsing to 4.38% in FY2024 (PAT falling to 812.58m) as the asset-quality shock described above took hold. Note the bank's own Directors'-Report-narrated ROE/ROA figures (e.g. 'Return on equity was 4.59% in 2021') are calculated on a Consolidated basis and will not match the Solo figures used here (Solo ROE 4.00% for FY2021) - this is an expected, documented difference in basis, not a data error (see sources.json).

Total assets grew every year of the 14-year series except FY2020, from 74,704.36m (FY2011) to 267,928.79m (FY2024), a 3.59x increase overall, with a single small contraction from 220,478.42m (FY2019) to 217,685.39m (FY2020, -1.27%) coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic year - driven mainly by the Investments-in-Shares-and-Securities book shrinking from 32,688.66m to 9,609.75m. Growth resumed the very next year and was never interrupted again, including through the FY2017 NPL spike and the FY2024 asset-quality shock.

historical_context: Standard Bank (renamed Standard Islami Bank PLC effective 10 February 2026) shows a 14-year public history in three phases. FY2011-FY2016: strong early profitability (ROE 19.59% falling steadily to 8.33%) on a rapidly growing but historically clean balance sheet (NPL ratio 2.19%-3.64%). FY2017-FY2020: a sharp NPL spike (3.64% to 8.29%) driven by a jump in classified loans from 3,799m to 10,451m, worked down over four years to 4.87% by FY2020 through disciplined recovery (verbatim-confirmed in that year's own Directors' Report) even as profitability kept compressing (ROE bottoming at 6.21% in FY2020) - a period that also includes the bank's shareholder-approved conversion from conventional to full-fledged Islamic banking (EGM 30 July 2020; Bangladesh Bank permission letter 24 Feb 2020), with the FY2021 annual report the first to drop conventional-banking terminology entirely. FY2021-FY2024: asset quality deteriorated again almost every year (NPL 6.19% to 7.94% to 7.27%) while general provisioning against unclassified investments dropped to nil for four consecutive years, culminating in FY2024's severe shock - classified investments quadrupling to 59,686.20m (29.96% of gross investments) with coverage collapsing to 13.12% and unprovided exposure reaching 2.80x total equity, while reported CRAR stayed flat only because of a Bangladesh-Bank-granted provisioning deferral disclosed in the bank's own report. Total assets grew in every year of the series except FY2020 (a small, COVID-19-linked -1.27% contraction, 220,478.42m to 217,685.39m), resuming growth the following year regardless of the credit cycle.
data_gaps: FY2013 has no annual report of its own (confirmed unobtainable - live site serves that era as opaque UUID downloads off a client-rendered list page; Wayback captures return a soft-404 app shell at HTTP 200) - recovered here at full audited-statement granularity from FY2014's own comparative column instead, with balance-sheet identity and PBT-tax=PAT both reproducing exactly. FY2012's own annual report has systematic PDF-to-text digit corruption affecting all large Taka figures; absolute Balance Sheet/P&L figures for FY2012 are instead taken from the FY2014 report's 5-year highlights table (equity/reserve split and non-interest-income breakdown are consequently unavailable for FY2012 only). FY2015's own report's summary table also extracted with heavy (though less severe) OCR corruption; its Balance Sheet/P&L are instead taken from FY2016's clean comparative column. FY2025 Q4/annual is confirmed to exist (27th AGM held 30 July 2026 approved the FY2025 audited financial statements) but is not yet retrievable as a structured document: the bank's own Annual Reports page lists only through FY2024, and dsebd.org's disclosure page gives only headline EPS/NAV/profit figures with no balance sheet or capital-adequacy detail - not fabricated into a full entry per project policy. EPS required cross-report/cross-source recovery in three years where the primary source's own field was illegible: FY2018 (from FY2019's comparative), FY2024 (from dsebd.org, with a ~1.9% cross-check gap against this dataset's own Solo PAT noted in sources.json). Tier-1/Tier-2/Risk-Weighted-Assets absolute Taka figures (as opposed to the CRAR percentage, which is available for all 14 years) are unavailable for FY2012, FY2013, FY2016 and FY2024 specifically - see sources.json for the year-specific reason in each case. Number of branches/employees/shareholders is only available from FY2012 and FY2014 onward (not FY2011, FY2013 or FY2015). The bank's own multi-year 'Five Year(s) Financial Highlights' tables are Consolidated-basis throughout (confirmed via repeated cross-checks against direct Solo statements) and were deliberately not used for any Balance Sheet or Profit-and-Loss aggregate in this dataset, only for classified-loan amounts, branch/employee/shareholder counts and market price - see sources.json for the full cross-check evidence. QUARTERLY (Q1-Q3) COVERAGE ADDED 2026-08-27: 39 of a possible 45 quarter-slots (2011-2025) now have genuine interim data -- see sources.json for the full per-quarter basis/provenance breakdown. Remaining quarterly gaps, all confirmed genuinely unrecoverable (not a research shortfall): FY2016 Q2 and FY2020 Q2 (no filing found on the live site, its CMS listing, or Wayback under any URL variant searched); FY2011 Q3 and FY2014 Q1 (a genuine filing PDF exists and was downloaded, but OCR quality on these two specific condensed-single-page scans was too unreliable to transcribe with confidence -- deliberately omitted per 'never fabricate', full technical detail and the recoverable source URL kept in sources.json for a future retry); FY2025 Q2 (full statement's only Wayback capture is truncated mid-file in a way that defeated pdfinfo/qpdf/mutool/PyMuPDF repair; a separate 1-page Price-Sensitive-Information disclosure survived but covers only Net Operating Cash Flow Per Share, not enough to construct a genuine entry); FY2025 Q3 (same truncation issue, no PSI fallback exists). Classified-investment/NPL/CAR figures are NOT available in the Q1-Q3 quarterly line_items (unlike the Q4/annual series) because this bank's own condensed interim filings do not disclose that level of asset-quality/capital-adequacy detail -- npl_ratio_pct, provision_coverage_pct and car_pct are therefore recorded as null for every Q1-Q3 period in ratios_timeseries.json, consistent with the same convention already used for CITYBANK's own Q1-Q3 entries.
